The Civil Judge, (Sr.Dn.), Bhadravathi, In The Interest
Of Justice And Etc.
 This Civil Petition, Coming On For Admission,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The captioned civil petition is filed by the petitioner - wife, who is a B.E Graduate, seeking transfer of divorce proceedings pending in M.C.No.63/2020 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mandya.

2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner - wife and learned counsel appearing for the respondent.
3.
The captioned civil petition is filed by the petitioner - wife alleging that on account of harassment and torture, she was compelled to return to her parental home at Bhadravathi.
The present petition is filed alleging NC: 2023:KHC:19200 that the respondent and his family members are highly influential and there is a threat to the petitioner's life.

She also pleads that she unable to travel from Bhadravthi to Mandya on each and every date of hearing and therefore, the present petition is filed seeking transfer.
4.

The petitioner also claims that she has already filed a civil miscellaneous petition seeking maintenance and a crime is also registered against the respondent - husband for the offence punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 in C.C.No.1779/2021.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent - husband countering the contentions raised by the petitioner - wife would bring to the notice of this Court that the petitioner - wife is employed at Bengaluru and that she is a B.E Graduate and the petition was filed at Mandya though she was employed and residing at Bengaluru.

It is borne out from the records coupled with the statement made by the learned counsels on record, the petitioner and the respondent were residing at Bengaluru when this petition was filed at Mandya.

2 7.

In the objection tendered by the respondent - husband, though has seriously objected for transfer of the proceedings from Bhadravthi to Mandya, however, having regard to the fact that the respondent - husband is also employed and staying at Bengaluru, the respondent - husband has no objection, if the divorce proceedings pending on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mandya are withdrawn and transferred to Bengaluru.
8. This statement is not countered by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner - wife.
On the contrary, the learned counsel would counter with the suggestion made by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent - husband.
On instructions, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that his client has no objection if divorce proceedings are withdrawn and transferred to the Family Court, Bengaluru.

10. In the light of the statement made by the learned counsel on record, I am of the view that if the divorce proceedings are withdrawn and transferred to the Family Court, Bengaluru, that may reduce the hardship to the petitioner - wife and she will be in a position to defend and contest the divorce proceedings.

11. In the light of the discussions made supra, I pass the following;
ORDER (i) The Civil Petition is allowed in part.

(ii) The proceedings pending in M.C. No.63/2020 pending on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, NC: 2023:KHC:19200 Mandya are withdrawn and transferred to the Family Court,
Bengaluru.

(iii) Since the parties are represented by their respective counsel, the petitioner and respondent are hereby directed to appear before the Family Court, Bengaluru on 10.07.2023 without expecting any further notice.
(iv) On receipt of intimation, the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mandya shall forthwith remit all the records to the Family Court, Bengaluru.
